title: Uber Ride Sharing: Complete Architecture
description: Design an Uber-like ride-sharing platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a ride-sharing platform like Uber. Riders request rides from their location, drivers accept requests and navigate to pickup, and the system matches them based on proximity, ETA, and driver rating. The platform must handle real-time location updates every 3 seconds, dynamic surge pricing, trip state management, and secure payment processing.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Rider: request ride with pickup/dropoff, select vehicle type (UberX, XL, Black), see upfront fare estimate
Driver: toggle online/offline, receive ride requests with accept/decline, navigate to pickup and dropoff
Real-time GPS location tracking for both rider and driver during active trip
Matching engine: assign nearest available driver using ETA, rating, and surge zone
Dynamic surge pricing based on supply-demand ratio per geohash zone
Trip state machine: requested -> driver_assigned -> arriving -> ongoing -> completed -> rated
Payment processing: authorize at start, capture at end, support split payment and tips
In-app navigation integration with traffic-aware ETAs (Google Maps, Mapbox)
Rider and driver ratings with 1-5 stars and optional feedback
Trip history with receipts, route replay, and support for lost items
Push notifications for ride status changes, driver messages, and payment confirmations
Safety features: share trip status with contacts, emergency button, driver background checks

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Sub-2s driver matching latency in metro areas
Real-time location updates every 3 seconds with < 500ms processing latency
99.99% availability for trip-critical services (matching, dispatch, payments)
Geospatial queries: find nearest 5 drivers in under 200ms using S2 or geohash indexing
Surge pricing calculation under 1 second per zone
Payment authorization within 2 seconds with PCI DSS compliance
Offline resilience: queue location updates and sync when connectivity returns
Cross-platform mobile apps with offline maps and cached trip state

data.text: Build a monolithic ASP.NET Core API with SQL Server and SignalR hub. Use SQL Server for users, trips, and payments. SignalR pushes real-time location updates and ride requests. Implement basic geospatial queries using SQL Server spatial types. This validates the trip lifecycle, driver dispatch, and payment capture flow.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - SignalR Hub for real-time location and ride events
  - Minimal API for REST endpoints
  - Entity Framework Core with SQL Server spatial types
  - Azure SQL Database for users, drivers, trips, payments
  - Azure Redis Cache for active ride sessions and location buffers
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service with WebSockets enabled
  - Azure Maps for geocoding and routing
  - Azure Service Bus for async payment and notification events
  - Single database with tables: Users, Drivers, Vehicles, Trips, Payments, Locations, SurgeZones

data.text: At scale, split into focused microservices. The Dispatch Service manages driver availability and ride requests, the Matching Engine computes optimal driver-rider pairs using geospatial indexes, the Trip Service manages the ride lifecycle, the Payment Service handles transactions, and the Location Service ingests and serves real-time GPS updates.

items: Dispatch Service: Manages driver online status, ride request queue per zone, and broadcasts available rides to nearby drivers via SignalR or WebSocket groups keyed by geohash.

Matching Engine: Runs ETA estimation using road-network distance (not straight-line), scores drivers on proximity, rating, acceptance rate, and vehicle type, then assigns the best match within 10 seconds.

Trip Service: Orchestrates the ride lifecycle via state machine (requested -> assigned -> enroute -> arrived -> ongoing -> completed), manages trip status transitions, and emits events for billing and notifications.

Payment Service: Handles payment authorization at ride start, capture at completion with dynamic fare calculation (distance, time, surge, tolls), supports split payments, tips, and refunds via Stripe or Braintree integration.

Location Service: Ingests high-frequency GPS pings from rider and driver apps (every 3s), stores recent location history in Redis geospatial indexes, and serves current positions to tracking maps with sub-second freshness.
Pricing Service: Calculates dynamic fares based on base rate, per-mile/minute pricing, surge multiplier per geohash zone, and demand forecasts using time-series models.

  shared/

Key Patterns:
  - Mapbox GL JS or Google Maps SDK for custom map rendering
  - WebSocket for real-time driver location and ride status
  - Background geolocation tracking with native app fallback
  - Optimistic UI for ride request with timeout rollback
  - Service Worker for offline trip state and map tiles

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Ride-sharing is real-time and geo-centric - optimize the matching path above all else
Use S2 or geohash for efficient nearest-driver queries; index on partition key
Separate location ingestion (high volume) from matching (low latency, high compute)
Payment and trip services must be strongly consistent; location and notifications can be eventual
Surge pricing requires fast time-series aggregation per zone with short TTLs
data.takeaway: Uber is a real-time geo-distributed system with strict latency requirements for matching and location. Use geospatial indexing for fast driver discovery, separate high-frequency location ingestion from low-latency matching, and maintain strong consistency only where financial or safety-critical state is involved.
